outcome: No progress on Serre's positivity conjecture (chi(R/P, R/Q) > 0 for proper intersections in a regular local ring) has been found since 26 January 2024; the conjecture remains open in general, with the same pre-2024 partial results (Gabber's non-negativity, Dutta 2008, Skalit 2019 for the two-dimensional-base case) still being the state of the art as of the current Wikipedia article.
summary: Serre's positivity conjecture states that for a commutative regular local ring R and prime ideals P, Q with dim(R/P) + dim(R/Q) = dim(R), the intersection multiplicity chi(R/P, R/Q) is strictly positive. I ran multiple searches (general web search and arXiv listings) for any 2024-2026 work on this exact statement and found none. All results returned either pre-2024 literature already known to be the state of the art (Gabber's proof of non-negativity via de Jong alterations, Gillet-Soule and Roberts on the vanishing part, S.P. Dutta's 2008 special case, C. Skalit's 2019/2015 result for rings essentially smooth over a two-dimensional regular base) or an unrelated problem with a similar name: the 'Grothendieck-Serre conjecture' on torsors/principal bundles under reductive group schemes over regular local rings (recent papers from 2024-2025 address this, e.g. arXiv:2412.11723 on the mixed-characteristic constant case), which is a completely different conjecture despite the shared 'Serre' + 'regular local ring' phrasing. I fetched the live Wikipedia article 'Serre's multiplicity conjectures' directly, which explicitly states the positivity property's 'proof for this property in the general case remains open,' and cites only the same pre-2024 partial results (Dutta 2008, Skalit 2019) with no new entries. I also searched specifically for any AI/Lean/formalization work touching intersection multiplicity conjectures and found none connected to this problem — only unrelated AI-math items (ABC conjecture attempt, a moduli-of-curves inequality, Frankl's conjecture in Lean) that do not concern Serre's positivity conjecture. I agree with the triage verdict of 'none.'
competing_reading: None. The only ambiguity is the shared 'Serre' name with the Grothendieck-Serre conjecture on torsors, but that problem concerns a structurally different question (existence of rational points / triviality of torsors under reductive group schemes) and is not a case or variant of the intersection-multiplicity positivity statement, so it was correctly excluded per the scope rule in §3.1.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or paper proving chi(R/P,R/Q) > 0 for proper intersections in the general (e.g. mixed-characteristic, ramified) case of a regular local ring, or extending the known cases (equicharacteristic, unramified mixed-characteristic, two-dimensional-base) to new settings, dated after 26 January 2024, together with expert digestion (e.g. in a survey, journal acceptance, or a mathematician's blog) to distinguish claimed from resolved status.
